mainTopic: Detaching a mushroom on שבת; which skins are fit for writing תפילין (bird, fish, kosher animals, נבלות); the story of רב, שמואל and קרנא; the start of the משנה on brine
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling: pulling a mushroom off a pitcher handle on שבת makes a person liable for עוקר דבר מגידולו, because that is where a mushroom naturally grows. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's words 'חיה ועוף'. רב הונא rules that תפילין may be written on kosher bird skin, and אביי explains that the feather holes do not disqualify it. רבי זירא and אביי then argue in two versions about whether the verse 'בכנפיו' shows that bird skin counts as real skin. Next, the גמרא explains why fish skin is doubtful for תפילין: the question is whether its foul smell ever goes away. A story follows in which קרנא tests רב with three questions: kosher parchment from 'בפיך', red blood from 'אדומים כדם', and the place of מילה from the word 'ערלתו'. The story ends with שמואל treating רב, and רב's curse on him comes true. The גמרא shows that the source for מילה is an argument between רבי יאשיה and רבי נתן. Then a ברייתא teaches that תפילין may be made from kosher animals, even נבלות and טרפות, and רבי יהושע הגרסי defends this to a ביתוסי. The amud ends with the start of a new משנה forbidding the making of brine on שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pulling a mushroom off a pitcher handle is liable
steps.stepSummary: Someone who detaches a mushroom growing on the handle of a pitcher is liable for the מלאכה of עוקר דבר מגידולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mushroom from the handle of a pitcher: he is liable for uprooting something from where it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling that began on the previous amud. Someone who pulls a mushroom off a pitcher's handle on שבת is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mushroom is not growing in the ground, but it is still treated as 'growing' where it is. Removing it counts as עוקר דבר מגידולו, which is a form of the מלאכה of reaping.

keyTerms.meaning: the handle (ear) of a pitcher or jug
uprooting something from its place of growth (a form of reaping)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'one who detaches' come right before it, on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: [One who detaches] a mushroom from the handle of a pitcher
phrases.notes: This sentence started on the previous amud and continues here.

phrases.english: is liable on account of
uprooting a thing from its place of growth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Detaching a mushroom from a pitcher handle on שבת carries liability for עוקר דבר מגידולו.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule of a sealed flowerpot
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא cites a ברייתא: picking from a perforated pot is liable, but picking from an unperforated pot is exempt. A pitcher handle is also not connected to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא objected: One who detaches from a perforated pot is liable, and from a non-perforated one he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא challenges the mushroom ruling. A plant in a sealed pot is not considered attached to the ground, and a pitcher is not attached to the ground either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot with a hole lets the plant draw from the earth, so the plant counts as growing. A sealed pot cuts the plant off from the ground, so picking from it is exempt. A pitcher handle seems even more cut off, so why should the mushroom count as growing?

keyTerms.meaning: a flowerpot with a hole in it

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya raised an objection:
One who detaches from a perforated pot is liable,
and from one that is not perforated, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that detaching a mushroom from a pitcher handle is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If something growing in a sealed pot is not considered 'growing' because it is cut off from the ground, a mushroom on a pitcher, which is also cut off from the ground, should not be either.

steps.title: Natural growth location makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: Plants do not naturally grow in sealed pots, but mushrooms naturally grow on things like pitcher handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, that is not its normal way of growing. Here, that is its normal way of growing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the test is whether this is the normal way the thing grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary plants normally grow in the ground, so a plant in a sealed pot is in an unnatural spot and does not count as attached. A mushroom normally grows on objects like this, so the pitcher handle is its real place of growth.
steps.whatToRemember: For עוקר דבר מגידולו, what matters is whether the thing is growing in its natural place. Physical connection to the ground is not the test.

phrases.english: There, that is not its normal way of growing;
here, that is its normal way of growing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by distinguishing the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are disconnected from the ground, so both should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The test is the thing's natural place of growth. A mushroom grows naturally on a pitcher, but a plant does not grow naturally in a sealed pot.

steps.title: תפילין may be written on kosher bird skin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites 'חיה ועוף' from the משנה, and רב הונא rules that תפילין may be written on the skin of a kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'An animal and a bird...' רב הונא said: We may write תפילין on the skin of a kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, about wounding an animal or bird on שבת. It brings רב הונא's ruling that a kosher bird's skin is valid for writing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is linked to bird skin because wounding means making a wound under the skin. רב הונא treats a bird's skin as real skin that can be made into parchment, as long as the bird is a kosher species.

keyTerms.meaning: a wild animal and a bird (quoted from the משנה)

phrases.english: [The Mishnah:] 'An animal and a bird, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about wounding on שבת, and a new topic starts here.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
We may write tefillin

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר שֶׁל עוֹף טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: on the skin of a kosher bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּה וָעוֹף כּוּ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic based on a different phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The skin of a kosher bird may be used for writing תפילין.

steps.title: What new point is רב הונא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what רב הונא adds. If the point is that birds have skin, the משנה already implies this by making someone who wounds a bird liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is he teaching us? That it has skin? We already learned: One who wounds them is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רב הונא's ruling as unnecessary, because the משנה seems to teach it already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for wounding means bleeding under the skin. If wounding a bird makes one liable, a bird must have skin. So רב הונא appears to be repeating what we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us (what is the new point)?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What is he teaching us?
That it has skin?
We already learned: One who wounds them is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 4 says anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling about writing on bird skin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's liability for wounding a bird already shows that a bird has skin, so רב הונא's statement adds nothing.

steps.title: The feather holes do not disqualify the skin
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רב הונא teaches a lot. Without him, we might think the feather holes make bird skin unfit for writing. The rule from ארץ ישראל is that a hole the ink passes over is not considered a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: He teaches us a lot. From the משנה alone I would have said that because it has many holes, it is not fit. So he teaches us, as they say in the West: Any hole that the ink passes over is not a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב הונא. Knowing that a bird has skin is not enough to know you can write תפילין on it, because of all the feather holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only proves that a bird has skin for the purpose of wounding. It does not show that skin full of holes is fit for writing. רב הונא teaches that tiny holes the ink simply crosses over do not count, following the rule from ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: in the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical rule for writing סת"ם: a tiny hole that the ink crosses without breaking the letter does not invalidate the writing.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
He teaches us a lot,
for if from the Mishnah alone, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית בֵּיהּ נִיקְבֵי נִיקְבֵי לָא,
phrases.english: since it has many holes, [one may] not [write on it];
so he teaches us, as they say in the West:
any hole that the ink passes over
is not a hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי טוּבָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a new point not covered by the earlier source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bird skin is real skin, but its feather holes would make it unfit for writing תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holes that the ink passes over do not count, so bird skin is fit for writing.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse 'by its wings'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא cites the teaching that 'בכנפיו' includes the bird's skin in what is burned on the altar. If it were real skin, why would the verse need to include it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: 'By its wings' comes to make the skin fit [for the altar]. If you think it is skin, how does the verse include it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the idea that a bird's skin counts as real skin, using a verse about the bird burnt-offering (עולת העוף).
steps.deeperAnalysis: With animal offerings, the skin is removed and not burned on the altar. If a bird's skin were real skin, it should follow the same rule. Since the verse says the bird's skin is burned, it seems a bird's skin is not considered real skin.

keyTerms.meaning: 'by its wings' (ויקרא א:יז, about the עולת העוף)
if it should enter your mind (if you assume)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
'By its wings' comes to make the skin fit [for the altar].
And if it should enter your mind that it is skin,
how does the verse include it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind steps 4 to 6 that bird skin counts as real skin.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a bird's skin is legally skin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real skin is not burned with an offering. Since the verse includes bird skin on the altar, it must not be real skin.

steps.title: It is skin, but the Torah included it anyway
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that bird skin really is skin, and the Torah made a special rule to include it on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It is skin, and the Torah included it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא: the verse does not prove that bird skin is not skin. The Torah simply made a special rule for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird skin stays in the category of skin. Burning it on the altar is a special exception for this offering, a גזירת הכתוב. It does not change the category.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It is skin, and the Torah included it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is a special decree, not a statement about the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Including the skin on the altar proves it is not real skin.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is real skin. The Torah made a special exception to include it on the altar.

steps.title: Second version: the verse proves bird skin is real skin
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי זירא uses the same verse as support. A verse is needed to include the skin only if it is real skin. If it were not skin, it would be burned with the meat anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי זירא said: We too have learned it: 'By its wings' comes to include the skin. If you say it is skin, that is why a verse was needed to include it. But if you say it is not skin, why was a verse needed to include it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי זירא's statement. Here he uses 'בכנפיו' as a proof that bird skin is skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is reversed from step 7. If bird skin is real skin, we would expect it to be removed like animal skin, so a verse is needed to include it. If it were just part of the meat, no verse would be needed, so the verse shows it is real skin.

keyTerms.meaning: we too have learned it (support from a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same verse but argue in opposite directions. In version one, רבי זירא says the verse shows bird skin is NOT skin. In version two, he says the verse shows it IS skin. In both versions, אביי takes the opposite side.

phrases.english: Some say: Rabbi Zeira said:
We too have also learned [this]:
'By its wings' comes to include the skin.
Granted, if you say it is skin,
that is why a verse was needed to include it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָאו עוֹר הוּא —
phrases.english: But if you say it is not skin,
why was a verse needed to include it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of step 7, in which רבי זירא supports the view instead of attacking it.
steps.raayaObject: That a bird's skin is legally skin, supporting רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'בכנפיו', which includes the skin of the עולת העוף.

steps.title: Not skin, but needed because the holes make it repulsive
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Bird skin might not be skin, and the verse would still be needed, because we might think the holes make it too repulsive for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Actually I can tell you it is not skin, and it was still needed. You might have thought that since it is full of holes, it is repulsive. So it teaches us [that it is offered].
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי זירא's proof by giving another reason the verse was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if bird skin counts as part of the meat, we might have thought its feather holes make it disgusting and unfit for the altar. The verse tells us it is still offered. So the verse does not prove that bird skin is real skin.

keyTerms.meaning: actually I can tell you (I keep my position)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'בכנפיו' can be read either way, so it does not decide whether bird skin is real skin. רב הונא's ruling that תפילין may be written on kosher bird skin is not rejected.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ לָאו עוֹר הוּא,
phrases.english: Actually, I can tell you that it is not skin,
and still it was needed:
it would have entered your mind to say

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית בֵּיהּ פִּירְצֵי פִּירְצֵי מְאִיס —
phrases.english: that since it has many holes, it is repulsive;
so it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ לָאו עוֹר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the verse. The ruling about writing on bird skin still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse could be needed for a different reason: the holes might have made the skin seem too repulsive for the altar.

steps.title: Can תפילין be written on kosher fish skin?
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא asks רב נחמן בר יצחק whether תפילין may be written on the skin of a kosher fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא asked רב נחמן בר יצחק: What is the law about writing תפילין on the skin of a kosher fish?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked. Is the skin of a kosher fish fit for writing תפילין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with bird skin and whether it counts as real skin. This question applies the same kind of thinking to fish. A kosher fish is a permitted food, so it might seem acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher)
תפילין, which must be written on fit parchment

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, asked
of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
What is the law about writing tefillin

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר שֶׁל דָּג טָהוֹר?
phrases.english: on the skin of a kosher fish?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bird skin to fish skin as a new writing surface.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether kosher fish skin is fit for writing תפילין.

steps.title: Only אליהו could decide
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that only אליהו could settle this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If אליהו comes and says.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the question cannot be settled now. Only אליהו הנביא could tell us the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a way of saying the matter depends on a fact we cannot know. The answer does not say what that fact is, which leads straight to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: If אליהו comes and says (an expression for something we cannot know right now)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְיֹאמַר.
phrases.english: He said to him: If Elijah comes and says.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְיֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about fish skin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The matter is undecided and depends on information only אליהו could supply.

steps.title: What exactly is in doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what doubt רב נחמן בר יצחק meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'If אליהו comes and says' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what fact we are missing that only אליהו could reveal. This sets up the next steps, which try out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'wait for אליהו' only makes sense if there is a specific unknown fact. The גמרא wants to identify that fact.

phrases.english: What does 'If Elijah comes and says' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the answer just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which unknown fact makes the fish-skin question undecidable.

steps.title: It can't be whether a fish has skin
steps.stepSummary: One idea is that the doubt is whether a fish has skin at all, but we can see that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the doubt is whether a fish has skin or does not have skin, we can see that it has skin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a first possible doubt: does a fish really have skin? It rejects this right away, because we can see with our own eyes that fish have skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody needs a prophet to settle something we can plainly see. So the doubt must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say: whether it has skin
or whether it does not have skin,
but we see that it has skin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes one meaning of the doubt and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the doubt is whether fish have skin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What we can see needs no אליהו to reveal it.

steps.title: A משנה shows fish skin counts as skin
steps.stepSummary: A further proof from a משנה shows that fish skin is treated as real skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, we learned: Fish bones and fish skin protect from impurity in a tent containing a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof that fish have real skin. A משנה treats fish skin as a covering that blocks impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish skin does not become impure itself, so it can act as a barrier against טומאת אהל. Because the משנה calls it 'skin' and gives it a legal role, the suggestion from the last step is ruled out even more firmly.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, we learned in a משנה
Protect, block impurity from reaching what is under them
A tent containing a dead body, which spreads impurity

phrases.english: And furthermore, we learned in a mishna:
fish bones and its skin
protect in a tent containing a corpse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָתְנַן: עַצְמוֹת הַדָּג וְעוֹרוֹ מַצִּילִין בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a written source to the proof from what we can see.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the doubt is whether fish have skin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already treats fish skin as skin.

steps.title: The doubt is whether the fish smell goes away
steps.stepSummary: The real doubt is whether the fish's foul smell ever fully leaves the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if אליהו comes and says whether its foul smell has left it or whether its foul smell has not left it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true meaning of the doubt. Fish skin is real skin, but we do not know whether its bad smell or oiliness ever completely goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the smell never leaves, the skin would not be fitting for תפילין. Whether processing removes the smell completely is something we cannot be sure about, so 'wait for אליהו.'
steps.whatToRemember: Fish skin is real skin. The question about using it for תפילין is only whether its foul smell ever fully goes away, and that is left undecided.

phrases.english: Rather: if Elijah comes and says
whether its foul smell has left it
or whether its foul smell has not left it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִם יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְיֹאמַר אִי פְּסַקָא זוּהֲמָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected meaning with the correct one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the doubt is whether fish have skin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fish clearly have skin. The doubt is whether the foul smell ever leaves it.

steps.title: שמואל senses a great scholar arriving
steps.stepSummary: While sitting by the river, שמואל sees the water rise and sends קרנא to test an arriving scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל and קרנא were sitting on the bank of נהר מלכא. They saw the water rising and murky. שמואל said to קרנא: A great man is coming from the West, and his stomach is aching, and the water is rising to greet him. Go sniff his jug (test what he knows).
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. It sets up the questions about writing and other matters that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rising water is taken as a sign honoring a great scholar from ארץ ישראל. 'Sniff his jug' means 'test what is inside him,' so קרנא is sent to check his learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A judge and scholar in בבל
Sniff his jug, test his knowledge

phrases.english: Shmuel and Karna were sitting
on the bank of the Malka River.
They saw that the water was rising and murky.
Shmuel said to Karna:
A great man is coming from the West
and his stomach is aching,
and the water is rising to greet him.
Go sniff his jug (test him).
phrases.notes: Meaning: find out what learning is inside him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל וְקַרְנָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי אַגּוּדָּא דִּנְהַר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story containing another source about which skins are fit for writing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל sends קרנא to test the arriving scholar.

steps.title: Why only kosher animal skin for תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: קרנא meets רב and asks for the source that תפילין may only be written on the skin of a kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found רב. He said to him: From where do we know that תפילין may be written only on the skin of a kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: קרנא finds the scholar, who turns out to be רב, and asks his first test question. It is about the rule for תפילין parchment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to the topic of the daf, which is what may be written on. The rule that only kosher animal skin is fit is taken as known, and קרנא wants its source.

phrases.english: He went and found Rav.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין תְּפִילִּין
phrases.english: He said to him: From where do we know that one does not write tefillin

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה?
phrases.english: except on the skin of a kosher animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The test announced in the story begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind the rule that תפילין must be written on kosher animal skin.

steps.title: From 'in your mouth': only what you may eat
steps.stepSummary: רב derives the rule from the verse 'so that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it is written, 'So that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth.' This means from what is permitted in your mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers with a verse from the פרשה of תפילין. Their parchment must come from an animal you are allowed to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links תפילין with 'your mouth.' רב reads this to mean that the material must come from something permitted to be put in your mouth, which is a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: From what is permitted in your mouth, meaning kosher to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard source for the halacha that סת״ם (Torah scrolls, תפילין and מזוזות) must be written on the skin of a kosher animal.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written:
'So that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth'
from what is permitted in your mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת ה׳ בְּפִיךָ״ — מִן הַמּוּתָּר בְּפִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first test question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'בפיך' teaches that only skin from something permitted to eat may be used.

steps.title: Why is the blood the Torah means red?
steps.stepSummary: קרנא asks for a source that the blood the Torah speaks of is red.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that blood is red?
steps.whatsHappening: This is קרנא's second test question. What color is the 'blood' the Torah refers to?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matters for the laws of נדה, where only certain shades of blood make a woman impure. קרנא wants a verse showing that 'blood' means a red color.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, here the blood relevant to the laws of impurity

phrases.english: From where do we know that blood is red?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second test question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse showing that 'blood' in the Torah means a red color.

steps.title: The water looked red like blood
steps.stepSummary: רב cites the verse saying the water looked 'red like blood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And מואב saw the water from afar, red like blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב quotes a verse from נביא. It compares red water to blood, which shows that blood is red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'red like blood' shows that the normal picture of blood is red. That defines which color counts as 'blood.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a verse)

phrases.english: As it says: 'And Moav saw from afar
the water, red like blood.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּרְאוּ מוֹאָב מִנֶּגֶד אֶת הַמַּיִם אֲדֻמִּים כַּדָּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second test question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison 'red like blood' proves that blood is red.

steps.title: How do we know where מילה is done?
steps.stepSummary: קרנא asks how we know that מילה is done on that specific place of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that circumcision is done on that place?
steps.whatsHappening: This is קרנא's third test question. The Torah says to cut the 'ערלה' but does not say where it is, so how do we know?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ערלה appears in several places in תנ״ך for different body parts and even for trees. So the specific location needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: On that place (a polite way to refer to the organ)

phrases.english: From where do we know that circumcision is on that place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third test question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for where מילה is performed.

steps.title: ערלתו compared to ערלתו of a tree
steps.stepSummary: רב links 'ערלתו' in מילה to 'ערלתו' of fruit trees, so מילה must be on the part that 'makes fruit'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'ערלתו' and it says there 'ערלתו.' Just as there it is something that makes fruit, so here it is something that makes fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב uses a גזירה שוה, which matches two verses that share the same word. The same word 'ערלתו' appears for a baby's מילה and for young fruit trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For trees, ערלה refers to something that produces fruit. So for מילה it must also be the body part that 'produces fruit,' meaning the one that produces children.

keyTerms.meaning: His or its ערלה, the word shared by both verses
It says here ... and it says there (the formula of a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: It says here 'his orlah,'
and it says there 'its orlah.'
Just as there it is something that produces fruit,
so too here it is something that produces fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the third test question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from ערלה of trees shows that מילה is done on the part that produces offspring.

steps.title: Why not the heart or the ear?
steps.stepSummary: קרנא challenges: the Torah also speaks of the 'ערלה' of the heart and of the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it is his heart, as it is written: 'And you shall circumcise the ערלת of your hearts'! Say it is his ear, as it is written: 'Behold, their ear is blocked (ערלה)'!
steps.whatsHappening: קרנא pushes back on רב's answer. Other verses use ערלה for the heart and the ear, so why not compare to those?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word ערלה is what links the verses, then the heart and ear verses could also be matched to מילה. This would give a different place for the מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a challenge offering another option)

phrases.english: Say it is his heart, as it is written:
'And you shall circumcise the orlah of your hearts'?!
Say it is his ear, as it is written:
'Behold, their ear is blocked'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לִבּוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמַלְתֶּם אֵת עׇרְלַת לְבַבְכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison just made.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's גזירה שוה linking מילה to trees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other verses also use ערלה for the heart and the ear, so why choose the tree verse?

steps.title: Match the full word only to the full word
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the full form 'ערלתו' is compared only to the same full form, not to forms that are attached to another word.
steps.simpleTranslation: We compare a full 'ערלתו' to a full 'ערלתו.' We do not compare a full 'ערלתו' to a 'ערלה' that is not full.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why the tree verse is the right match. Only the tree verse uses the exact same full word 'ערלתו,' just like the מילה verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heart and ear verses use ערלת and ערלה, which are attached to another word ('your hearts,' 'their ear'). The word 'ערלתו' stands on its own in both the מילה verse and the tree verse, so those two are matched together.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete, the full word standing on its own
Not complete, a form attached to another word

steps.confusionAlert: 'תמה' here does not mean 'surprising.' It means 'complete,' meaning the word 'ערלתו' appears in its full form standing on its own.

phrases.english: We compare a complete 'orlaso'
to a complete 'orlaso,'
and we do not compare a complete 'orlaso'
to an 'orlah' that is not complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the גזירה שוה against the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any verse using ערלה could be compared, including the heart and the ear.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the identical full form ערלתו is compared, and that is found in the tree verse.

steps.title: רב reacts to קרנא's name
steps.stepSummary: Seeing that he was being tested, רב asks קרנא's name and answers with a wordplay on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is your name? קרנא. He said to him: May it be the will (of ה׳) that a horn (קרנא) come out in his eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רב realizes קרנא was testing him and responds with a sharp play on the name קרנא, which means 'horn.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was bothered by being tested this way, and his words were a curse on קרנא, playing on his name, which means 'horn.' This closes the testing episode, and the next step finishes the story with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: May it be the will (of ה׳)
A horn in his eye, a wordplay on the name קרנא

steps.whatToRemember: In this story רב gives three sources: kosher-animal parchment for תפילין from 'בפיך,' blood is red from 'אדומים כדם,' and the place of מילה from the matching word 'ערלתו.'

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your name?
Karna.
He said to him: May it be the will of ה׳
that a horn come out in his eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after the three test questions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The test ends with רב's sharp reaction to having been tested.

steps.title: שמואל treats רב, and רב's curse comes true
steps.stepSummary: שמואל feeds רב healing foods and does not show him the bathroom. רב, upset by the suffering, curses whoever is troubling him, and the curse comes true.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, שמואל brought רב into his house. He fed him barley bread and small fried fish and gave him beer to drink. He did not show him where the bathroom was, so that רב would have diarrhea and his stomach would be cleared out. רב cursed and said: 'Whoever is making me suffer, may his children not survive.' And that is what happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רב and שמואל ends. שמואל tries to heal רב's stomach, but רב does not realize this and curses him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was a doctor. The foods and the missing bathroom were meant to flush out רב's sick stomach. רב only felt the pain and did not know the plan, so he cursed the person causing it. The גמרא tells us the curse came true, which shows how powerful the words of a great person are, even when said by mistake.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of רב and שמואל ends sadly: רב's curse, said without knowing שמואל meant well, came true.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל was not being cruel. He was acting as a doctor, and holding back the bathroom was part of the treatment.

phrases.english: In the end, Shmuel brought him into his house
he fed him barley bread
and small fried fish
and gave him beer to drink
and did not show him the bathroom
so that he would have diarrhea
phrases.notes: This would clear out his stomach and heal him.

phrases.english: Rav cursed and said:
Whoever is making me suffer
may his children not survive
And so it was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of רב's meeting with שמואל and קרנא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's curse against the person who made him suffer came true, even though שמואל meant to heal him.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה learns the place of מילה from the word ערלתו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רב's source is really one side of an argument between תנאים. רבי יאשיה learns 'ערלתו' in מילה from 'ערלתו' in fruit trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches an argument between תנאים. How do we know that מילה is done on that part of the body? The Torah says 'ערלתו' here (about מילה), and it says 'ערלתו' there (about fruit trees). Just as there it means something that makes fruit, here too it means something that makes fruit. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question of where מילה is done. It shows that רב's answer from step 23 is exactly the view of the תנא רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כתנאי' tells us that the question is really an argument between earlier Sages. רבי יאשיה uses a comparison of words: 'ערלתו' about a tree refers to something that makes fruit. So 'ערלתו' about a person must also refer to the part that 'makes fruit', meaning has children.

keyTerms.meaning: this matches an argument between תנאים
its or his 'orlah' (foreskin, or the fruit of a young tree)

phrases.english: This matches an argument between Tannaim:
How do we know that circumcision is done in that place?
It says here, 'his orlah'
and it says there, 'its orlah'
phrases.notes: About the fruit of a young tree

phrases.english: Just as there it is something that makes fruit
so too here it is something that makes fruit
These are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא returns to קרנא's question and brings a source from the תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יאשיה: מילה is on the part of the body that 'makes fruit'. He learns this by comparing the word 'ערלתו' to its use for fruit trees.

steps.title: רבי נתן learns it from the word 'זכר'
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the word comparison is not needed. The verse says 'an uncircumcised male', so מילה is on the part that shows the difference between male and female.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: this is not needed. The verse already says, 'And an uncircumcised male who does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin'. So מילה is on the place that shows whether someone is male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן gives a different source for the same rule. He uses a simpler reading of the verse instead of a word comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree on where מילה is done. They only argue about how we know it. רבי נתן reads the word 'זכר' (male) as pointing to the body part that makes a person male.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי נתן does not disagree about the halacha. He only disagrees about the source for it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: This is not needed
since the verse says
'And an uncircumcised male who does not circumcise'
'the flesh of his foreskin'
the place that shows the difference between male and female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source than רבי יאשיה for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נתן: the word 'זכר' alone shows that מילה is on the male organ.
steps.whatToRemember: Two תנאים agree on where מילה is done but learn it differently: רבי יאשיה from 'ערלתו', רבי נתן from 'זכר'.

steps.title: Which hides may be used for תפילין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that תפילין may be written on the hide of a kosher animal, even a נבלה or טרפה. They may be wrapped with its hair and sewn with its sinews, which is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: we may write תפילין on the hide of a kosher farm animal, on the hide of a kosher wild animal, and even on the hides of their נבלות and טרפות. The תפילין may be wrapped with their hair and sewn with their sinews. It is a הלכה למשה מסיני that תפילין are wrapped with their hair and sewn with their sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא about which animal hides may be used to make תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the kind of animal, not how it died. So even a kosher animal that became a נבלה or טרפה may be used. The rule about hair and sinews comes from a tradition given to משה at Sinai.

keyTerms.meaning: animals that died without proper שחיטה, or that had a fatal defect
a law given orally to משה at Sinai

phrases.english: The Sages taught: We may write tefillin
on the hide of a kosher farm animal
and on the hide of a kosher wild animal

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר נְבֵלוֹת וּטְרֵפוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶן.
phrases.english: and on the hides of their neveilot and tereifot.
And they may be wrapped with their hair and sewn with their sinews
and it is a law given to Moshe at Sinai
that tefillin are wrapped with their hair and sewn with their sinews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new related topic, another source showing what makes a material fit for a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין may be written on the hide of any kosher animal, including a נבלה or טרפה, and are wrapped and sewn with its hair and sinews.

steps.title: Hides of non-kosher animals may not be used
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: we may not write תפילין on the hide of a non-kosher animal, and certainly not on its נבלה or טרפה. We also may not use its hair or sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we may not write on the hide of a non-kosher farm animal, or on the hide of a non-kosher wild animal. It goes without saying that we may not write on the hide of their נבלה or טרפה. And we may not wrap the תפילין with their hair or sew them with their sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side of the rule: what may not be used for תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal may never be used, whether it was slaughtered or not. Since even the 'best' non-kosher animal is not allowed, its נבלה or טרפה is surely not allowed either.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין כּוֹתְבִין לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: But we may not write on the hide of a non-kosher farm animal

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר חַיָּה טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: nor on the hide of a non-kosher wild animal
and it goes without saying

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר נְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה שֶׁלָּהֶן.
phrases.english: not on the hide of their neveilah or tereifah.
And they may not be wrapped with their hair
and may not be sewn with their sinews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same ברייתא, listing what is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No part of a non-kosher animal may be used to make תפילין.

steps.title: A ביתוסי asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: A ביתוסי asks רבי יהושע הגרסי how we know that תפילין may not be written on the hide of a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the question that a ביתוסי asked רבי יהושע הגרסי: How do we know that we do not write תפילין on the hide of a non-kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a story. Someone asks for the Torah source of the rule we just learned, which sets up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ביתוסים did not accept the Oral Torah, so he wants a source in the written verses. The question is about the source, not about whether the rule is true.

keyTerms.meaning: a Boethusian, a member of a group that rejected the Oral Torah
how do we know? what is the source?

phrases.english: And this is the question a certain Boethusian asked
Rabbi Yehoshua HaGarsi:
How do we know that we do not write tefillin
on the hide of a non-kosher animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule from step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for not using non-kosher hides for תפילין.

steps.title: Only from what is permitted in your mouth
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the verse says 'so that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth', which means only from something you are allowed to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'So that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth.' This means it must come from something that is permitted in your mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע הגרסי answers with a verse about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In your mouth' is read as 'something your mouth may eat'. So the material for תפילין must come from a kind of animal that is kosher to eat.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'So that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth'
from something that is permitted in your mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת ה׳ בְּפִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'בפיך' teaches that תפילין must come from an animal permitted to eat.

steps.title: Then נבלות and טרפות should also be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ביתוסי challenges: a נבלה or טרפה may not be eaten either, so by this logic its hide should not be used for תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תפילין should not be written on the hides of נבלות and טרפות!
steps.whatsHappening: The ביתוסי attacks the answer by showing it seems to contradict the ברייתא, which allows נבלות and טרפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is 'only what you may eat', then a kosher animal that died without שחיטה is also not allowed in your mouth. Yet the ברייתא allows its hide, so the answer seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so, from now on (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But if so,

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹר נְבֵלוֹת וּטְרֵפוֹת אַל יִכָּתְבוּ!
phrases.english: they should not be written on the hides of neveilot and tereifot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 33.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נבלות and טרפות are forbidden to eat, yet the ברייתא allows their hides, so 'what is permitted to eat' cannot be the test.

steps.title: The parable of the king and the executioner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with a parable: a person killed by the king himself is more honored than one killed by an executioner. An animal that died 'by Heaven' is not worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I will give you a parable. What is this like? Like two people who were sentenced to death by the government. One was killed by the king himself, and one was killed by the executioner. Which one is more honored? You must say: the one the king killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע defends his answer by explaining why a נבלה is not a lower-quality animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that dies by itself was 'killed by the King', meaning ה׳, while a slaughtered animal was killed by a person. So a נבלה is not worse. The verse's test is the kind of animal, not how it died, and a נבלה of a kosher kind still counts as a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: I will give you a parable

phrases.english: He said to him: I will give you a parable
What is this like?
Like two people
who were sentenced to death by the government
One was killed by the king
and one was killed by an executioner
Which of them is more honored?
You must say: the one the king killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parable that redefines the status of a נבלה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נבלה is worse than a slaughtered animal, so it should be disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נבלה died 'by the King' and is not inferior; it is still a kosher kind of animal.

steps.title: Then נבלות should be eaten
steps.stepSummary: The ביתוסי pushes back: if a נבלה is so honored, it should be allowed to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, they should be eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: The ביתוסי challenges the parable by taking it one step further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dying 'by the King' makes the animal better, then a נבלה should be even better than a slaughtered animal, and it should be allowed as food.

phrases.english: But if so, they should be eaten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the parable of step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a נבלה is not inferior.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a נבלה is more honored, there is no reason it should be forbidden to eat.

steps.title: The Torah itself forbade eating it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers: the Torah clearly says 'do not eat any נבלה', so eating it is forbidden by decree, not because the animal is lower in quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Torah said, 'Do not eat any נבלה', and you say they should be eaten?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers the last challenge by pointing to a clear verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not eating a נבלה is a direct command of the Torah. It does not show that the animal is of lower quality. So for תפילין, the kind of animal is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: do not eat any animal that died without שחיטה

phrases.english: He said to him: The Torah said
'Do not eat any neveilah'
and you say they should be eaten?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit verse as a Torah decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a נבלה is not inferior, it should be permitted to eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating it is forbidden only because of a direct verse, not because it is inferior.

steps.title: The ביתוסי agrees: well said
steps.stepSummary: The ביתוסי accepts the answer and says 'קאלוס', meaning 'well said'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Well said!
steps.whatsHappening: The debate ends with the questioner admitting that the answer is good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source 'what is permitted in your mouth' stands. It refers to the kind of animal, so a kosher נבלה is fine for תפילין while any non-kosher animal is not.
steps.whatToRemember: תפילין must come from a kosher kind of animal ('מותר בפיך'). How the animal died does not matter, so a kosher נבלה or טרפה may be used.

phrases.english: He said to him: Well said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The questioner accepts the answer of step 37.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source 'בפיך' is accepted: תפילין may be made only from kosher kinds of animals, including their נבלות and טרפות.

steps.title: New משנה: No making brine on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the rule that one may not make הילמי (strong salt water) on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: You may not make brine (very salty water) on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a simple rule: you may not make הילמי, a strong salt water, on שבת. This opening line sets up the rest of the משנה, which will explain what is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh topic and has no link to the story about the ביתוסי. The rule only forbids making a strong brine. The rest of the משנה, on the next amud, will spell out how a weaker salt water may still be made.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
Brine, meaning very salty water used for pickling or soaking food.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this means all salt water is forbidden on שבת. Only strong brine, the kind used for pickling, is forbidden. The rest of the משנה allows a milder salt water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source for the halachos of preparing salt water on שבת, which people still deal with today, for example the salt water at the Seder table.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may not make brine on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: הילמי is strong salt water used for pickling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the story of רבי יהושע and the ביתוסי ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making strong brine (הילמי) on שבת is forbidden.
